blocks.text: Managing compensation data in Excel on Mac

Your daily work involves pulling data from HRIS systems and normalizing it for analysis. Excel is often the bridge between raw data and actionable insights. When working on a Mac, you need to be aware of how Microsoft 365 interacts with macOS. Performance issues often stem from large workbooks with complex nested functions.
Practical Excel tips for compensation analysts

items: Use XLOOKUP instead of VLOOKUP for better performance and flexibility when searching for employee data.
Freeze panes to keep header rows visible while scrolling through large salary datasets.
Use data validation to create drop-down menus for job levels or department codes to prevent entry errors.
Learn the keyboard shortcuts like Command + T to quickly turn a range into an official Excel table.
Use conditional formatting to instantly highlight pay equity outliers or employees outside their salary range.

blocks.text: Many organizations still rely on manual spreadsheets for annual merit cycles. This leads to version control issues and high error rates. While specialized tools like Pave or Workday Compensation exist, Excel remains the tool of choice for ad-hoc modeling. Keep your workbooks clean by separating data inputs from your calculation layers.

Mac users often find that Windows-based keyboard shortcuts conflict with macOS system commands. You may need to visit System Settings > Keyboard > Shortcuts to disable or reassign conflicting keys. Also, ensure you are running the latest version of Excel for Mac, as Microsoft regularly releases performance updates for Apple Silicon chips.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur to edit my Excel files directly?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not edit files or click buttons for you. It provides guidance, answers questions, and dictates text so you can work faster.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with Microsoft 365 on Mac?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur works in any app on macOS, including Excel, by looking at your screen and listening to your voice commands.

faq.question: How do I handle large datasets in Excel on Mac?
faq.answer: Use Power Query for data transformation and ensure your Mac has at least 8 GB of RAM to handle complex calculations.
